newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia soldier gets death sentence for shooting.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia soldier gets death sentence for shooting.

text.p: A junior officer from Indonesia's special forces has been sentenced to death for killing 16 people in a shooting spree last year in remote Irian Jaya province, a military spokesman said on Wednesday.
"He was sentenced to death by the military tribunal on Tuesday, but appealed against the sentence," Captain Edi Sulistiadi told Reuters from the provincial capital Jayapura.
"The next hearing will be held soon at the high military tribunal in Surabaya, East Java but no date has been set," he added.

The officer, Second Lieutenant Sumorip of the Kopassus elite forces, was convicted of killing 16 people and wounding 10 others at the airport in Timika town last April. Military prosecutor Colonel Balukia on Monday demanded the death penalty for the 37-year-old soldier.

The dead included Sumorip's commanding officer and three fellow Kopassus soldiers. Other soldiers and four civilians, including a New Zealand pilot working in Irian Jaya, were also killed in the two-hour shooting spree, newspapers reported at the time.
Military prosecutors have said Sumorip may have been spurred to violence over frustration with his assignments.

"He had been told that he will be a deputy commander of a unit during his posting. On the other hand, he was assigned to help build a helicopter pad and markets...this apparently had made him frustrated," Sulistiadi said.
